in a cohort of 237 HIV- 1 seropositives in Dar es Salaaman, Tanzania, 13 of the 50 who had at least 3 CD4+ determinations and were followed up for at least 5 years were long-term slow CD4 progressors, defined as maintaining a CD4 slope of -10 or less.

1/3 of HIV-1 infected individuals in a cohort of 237 antiretrovinal naïve individuals in Tanzania had a slow progression of HIV- 1 infection, and that a large number of individuals with a low baseline CD4 count could be LTSP.
26.0% of the study population were LTSP, with a median CD4 cell slope of −9.5 cells/y, and a median time from HIV-1 infection to CD4 cell count below 500 cells/µL of 9.0 y.

the identification and characterization of LTSP in an African setting.
the identification of a group of individuals who are able to maintain a CD4+ T cell count ≥500 cell/µl for >5 years, or who maintain a CD4 cell slope ≤ − 10.
the natural history of the HIV-1 infection.

a large proportion of HIV-1 infected individuals with low CD4+ cells at baseline have a slow CD4 cell progression.
